name: Algorytm
classification_notes: Modern sans-serif rooted in early American Gothic types – Times Gothic, Inland Gothic N6 and Gothic N2. Organised as a six-family system (Algorytm, Clear, Soft, Sport, Flip, Mono) totalling 51 styles. The Flip subfamily inverts contrast for branding use. Rich alternates throughout; released April 2026 still at Beta 0.1 status.
summary: A six-family sans-serif system rooted in early American Gothic types, spanning display, text, mono, sport and reverse-contrast variants with full Latin and Cyrillic support.
description: Algorytm draws on early American Gothic typefaces – Times Gothic, Inland Gothic N6 and Gothic N2 – as the basis for a modern, systematically organised collection. Six related subfamilies cover the main use cases: standard display (Algorytm), extended reading (Clear), rounded and approachable (Soft), dynamic inline (Sport), reverse-contrast branding (Flip) and monospaced (Mono), all sharing eight weights with italics. The character sets are notably deep, with multiple stylistic alternates per key letter, text and lining numerals, a mathematical symbol set, and consistent Cyrillic coverage throughout.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type describes Algorytm as a versatile collection of sans-serif families inspired by early Gothic types, combining a modern aesthetic with a systematic approach. The design prioritises multifunctionality, diversity and flexibility, offering an abundance of alternates, features and special characters to serve needs from corporate identity to craft beverage packaging.

name: Algorytm Clear
classification_notes: Text-optimised member of the Algorytm system, rooted in early American gothic models (Times Gothic, Inland Gothic). Neutral grotesque with a generous alternate set: one-storey and two-storey 'a', geometric and standard variants for 'f', 'g', 'r', 't', 'y', 'G', 'I', 'R', and Cyrillic 'К' and 'Ж'. Currently released as Beta 0.1.
summary: A text-optimised grotesque drawn from early American gothic models, offering six weights with italics, Cyrillic support and a generous set of stylistic alternates.
description: Algorytm Clear is the legibility-first member of Interval Type's Algorytm system, designed to serve body text where the display-weight variant steps back. It draws on early American gothics – Times Gothic and Inland Gothic – for its proportions, updated with a systematic approach and an extensive alternate set covering single and double-storey forms across multiple glyphs. Six weights from Extralight to Bold, each with a matching italic, make it broadly usable for editorial work, though its Beta 0.1 status warrants caution in production.
foundry_blurb: Algorytm Clear is part of the Algorytm collection, a versatile sans-serif system inspired by early gothics such as Times Gothic and Inland Gothic. While the standard Algorytm makes a bold statement at larger sizes, Clear is tailored for legibility in extended text passages. It includes comprehensive stylistic alternates and supports both Extended Latin and Cyrillic scripts.

name: Algorytm Flip
classification_notes: Reverse contrast companion within the six-family Algorytm collection. Inspired by early American gothic display faces – Times Gothic, Inland Gothic N6, Gothic N2 – with stroke weight deliberately inverted: horizontals thicken, verticals thin. Eight weights from Extralight to Ultra. Extended Latin and Cyrillic with character-level OpenType alternates for both scripts.
summary: A reverse contrast companion to the Algorytm collection, drawing from early American gothic references and spanning eight weights with Cyrillic support.
description: Algorytm Flip inverts the conventional stroke hierarchy of a sans-serif, thickening horizontals and thinning verticals to create a typographic tension suited to display and branding work. Part of a six-family system built on gothic references including Times Gothic and Inland Gothic N6, it brings structural rigour to a deliberately unconventional premise. Eight weights from Extralight to Ultra, with extensive OpenType alternates across both Latin and Cyrillic.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type describes Algorytm as a versatile collection of sans-serif families inspired by early gothic display types, built for multifunctionality, diversity and flexibility. Algorytm Flip is the reverse contrast member of the six-family system, sitting alongside standard, clear, soft, mono and sport variants.

name: Algorytm Mono
classification_notes: Fixed-width sans-serif from the six-family Algorytm system, rooted in early American gothic faces – Times Gothic and Inland Gothic N6. Carries the collection's systematic design language into monospaced contexts with OpenType alternates, mathematical symbols and Cyrillic coverage. Gothic origins give it more character than a utilitarian code font.
summary: A six-weight monospaced sans-serif from Interval Type's Algorytm system, grounded in early American gothic sources with genuine Cyrillic support and a broader set of OpenType alternates than most code fonts carry.
description: Algorytm Mono is the fixed-width member of Ilya Naumoff's Algorytm collection – a six-family, 51-style system drawing from Times Gothic and Inland Gothic N6. It runs Extralight to Bold and brings the family's design language into code and tabular contexts, with one-storey 'a' variants, four 'y' alternates, Cyrillic letter swaps, circled numerals and mathematical symbols. The Cyrillic coverage and historical grounding lift it clear of the generic code-font category.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type describes the Algorytm collection as built for multifunctionality and flexibility – a system that can serve a tech corporate identity or a craft beer label from the same design vocabulary. Algorytm Mono is the code-ready member of that system, designed to carry the family's graphic character into fixed-width settings without becoming purely utilitarian.

name: Algorytm Soft
classification_notes: Part of the six-family Algorytm Collection (51 styles in total). Draws from early American gothic types — Times Gothic, Inland Gothic N6 and Gothic N2 — and applies rounded corners throughout to produce a warmer, less austere register than the base Algorytm. Extensive stylistic alternates cover single- and double-storey 'a', multiple 'y' variants, geometric 'f', 'r' and 't' options, and dedicated Cyrillic alternates for К and Ж. Extended Latin and Cyrillic support.
summary: The rounded member of Interval Type's Algorytm Collection, softening early American gothic structure into a warm geometric sans with eight weights, rich OpenType alternates and dual Latin/Cyrillic coverage.
description: Algorytm Soft shares the historical DNA of the broader Algorytm Collection — drawn from Times Gothic, Inland Gothic N6 and Gothic N2 — but rounds every corner to shift the typeface into a friendlier, more approachable register. Eight weights from Extralight to Ultra give it genuine range, and a generous set of stylistic alternates (multiple 'a', 'y' and 'g' variants, plus dedicated Cyrillic options) lets designers fine-tune its character to the job. It sits within a coherent six-family system, so tone can be shifted without abandoning the underlying visual language.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type presents Algorytm Soft as the friendly voice within the Algorytm Collection — a rounded-corner variant built to soften and warm the family's tone. The collection draws on early sans serif types and is designed as a flexible, systematic toolbox: six families across 51 styles, suited to everything from headline impact to body text, with extended Latin and Cyrillic support throughout.

name: Algorytm Sport
classification_notes: An inline variant within the broader Algorytm sans-serif family. The inline treatment – hairline strokes cut through bold letter bodies – places it firmly in display territory despite its gothic sans-serif origins. Draws on early American gothic faces: Times Gothic, Inland Gothic N6, Gothic N2.
summary: An inline display sans from Interval Type's Algorytm collection, using hairline strokes inside bold gothic-inspired letterforms to produce high-energy display headlines.
description: Algorytm Sport is the decorative member of Ilya Naumoff's six-family Algorytm collection, distinguished by inline letterforms drawn from early American gothic faces including Times Gothic and Inland Gothic N6. The inline treatment is strictly display-grade, making it suited to sports branding, packaging and poster headlines rather than extended reading. Extended Latin and Cyrillic are covered in a single Regular weight.
foundry_blurb: Algorytm Sport is the standout member of the Algorytm family, embodying a vibrant and healthy appearance. Lively inline letters inject energy into layouts. Part of the wider Algorytm collection – six type families totalling 51 styles – inspired by early gothic typefaces and built for multifunctionality, diversity and flexibility across corporate identity, packaging and beyond.

name: Englisch
classification_notes: Contemporary display family drawing on 17th and 18th century English sources – Fell Types and Caslon are the primary references. High vertical contrast and open forms are carried through a modern expressive lens rather than as a strict revival. The eccentricity is intentional and controlled, not incidental.
summary: A high-contrast display family that channels the eccentric energy of Fell Types and Caslon into something unmistakably contemporary, with six weights and matching italics across 12 styles.
description: Designed by Ilya Naumoff at Paris-based Interval Type, Englisch takes 17th and 18th century English typography – Fell Types and Caslon chief among its references – as a starting point rather than a destination. The result is a display family with real vertical contrast and open forms that read confidently at large sizes, inflected with a deliberate rhythmic eccentricity that keeps it from feeling like a revival. It won a TDC award in 2022, and the recognition feels earned.
foundry_blurb: Englisch draws inspiration from the typography of 17th and 18th century England, evoking historic faces such as Fell Types and Caslon. Rather than a strict revival, it offers a contemporary interpretation of key elements from that era, embracing eccentricity, vertical contrast and open forms, with design nuances that introduce a sense of playful rhythm. Suited to impactful titles and logos across print and web.

name: Factor A Mono
classification_notes: Monospaced companion to the Factor A proportional family. Low-contrast geometric grotesk construction with equal cap and ascender heights. Retains the family's warmth through the double-storey 'a' and a classic 't' form. A hand-drawn loop concept enables the range of character alternates across four stylistic sets. Extended Latin and Cyrillic coverage.
summary: The monospaced companion to Factor A, in five weights with Cyrillic support and four stylistic sets covering a clean default, rounded lowercase and coding-friendly 'i' and 'l' alternates.
description: Factor A Mono brings the proportional family's low-contrast geometric construction into fixed-width territory, with five weights from Ultralight to Bold and coverage of extended Latin and Cyrillic. Four stylistic sets offer a neutral default, a rounded lowercase option, a more expressive 'Funk It Up' variant and an alternative set with clearer 'i' and 'l' differentiation for coding contexts. Equal cap and ascender heights, the double-storey 'a' and the classic 't' tie it directly to the wider Factor A system.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type describes Factor A Mono as a functional geometric grotesk drawing on early 20th-century sans serif design. The foundry points to the balance of cold geometric structure with warmth through the double-storey 'a' and a somewhat classic 't', alongside a hand-drawn loop concept that makes the range of character alternates possible.

name: Factor A Variable
classification_notes: Functional geometric grotesk drawing on early 20th-century sans serif traditions. Low contrast with cap height matching ascender height. Warmth is introduced through a double-storey 'a' and a classic 't' form rather than through stroke modulation. A "hand-drawn loop" concept underlies a set of decorative alternates for headlines; the default character set reads cleanly in text. Updated in 2023 to a three-axis variable font covering weight, width and a third axis, with 56 static styles across four width variants.
summary: A carefully considered geometric grotesque with genuine warmth, strong Cyrillic coverage, and a thorough three-axis variable implementation spanning 56 styles across four widths.
description: Factor A threads warmth into geometric grotesque conventions through deliberate letterform choices – a double-storey 'a', a classic 't' – rather than through contrast or humanist influence. A set of decorative alternates based on a hand-drawn loop concept gives headline work personality without compromising the clean default for body copy. The 2023 variable update consolidated 56 styles (seven weights, four widths, with italics) into a single three-axis file, and the Cyrillic coverage makes it genuinely useful across multilingual projects.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type describes Factor A as a functional geometric grotesk that synthesises the sans serif designs of the early 20th century. Despite the cold geometry typical of the style, the typeface retains warmth through a double-storey 'a' and a somewhat classic 't'. A large choice of alternates, enabled by the concept of the hand-drawn loop, can be used to liven up titles and logos, while the default style works for extended text.

name: Factor B
classification_notes: Geometric grotesque drawing on Futura and early 20th-century sans-serifs, including Johnston Sans, as conceptual anchors. Deliberately more rational in construction than its sibling Factor A, yet varied cap and ascender heights prevent it from reading as purely mechanical. The Altiverse OpenType alternate set introduces a second register of geometrically constructed letterforms, partly influenced by analogue synth-era typography, intended for display and logotype work. No italic or condensed variants.
summary: A considered geometric grotesque with a disciplined default set and an expressive Altiverse alternate system that shifts its register entirely for display and logotype work.
description: Factor B is a six-weight geometric grotesque by Ilya Naumoff of Interval Type, drawing on Futura and Johnston Sans without copying either. Its default character set reads as clean and neutral across display and text sizes; the Altiverse alternate system, built from geometrically structured forms with a nod to analogue synth-era lettering, gives designers a second, more characterful mode for headlines and identities. Extended Latin and Cyrillic coverage make it a practical workhorse beyond its expressive ambitions.
foundry_blurb: Factor B is described by Interval Type as a functional and reliable geometric grotesque, conceptually inspired by Futura and its alternates, and synthesising early 20th-century sans-serif design including Johnston Sans. The default character set is neutral and highly legible; the Altiverse set offers a wide selection of geometrically constructed alternates suited to titles and logos. It operates effectively at both display and text sizes and includes extended Cyrillic support.

name: Oceanic
classification_notes: Upright-contrast serif inspired by 18th–19th-century fat faces (Bodoni, Canon, Scotch Roman). Lowercase c and e carry creature-like forms; R and K are drawn with deliberate tension. A Display variant maximises these qualities at scale; a Text subfamily reduces contrast and condenses slightly for continuous reading. Covers Extended Latin and Cyrillic across six weights with matching italics.
summary: A high-contrast serif rooted in fat face tradition, with creature-like letterform details and a Text subfamily that earn it a place well beyond the headline.
description: Oceanic draws from the upright contrast of 18th and 19th-century fat faces – Bodoni, Canon, Scotch Roman – but pushes into idiosyncratic territory: the c and e suggest prehistoric sea creatures, and the R and K are cut with deliberate tension. A Display variant leans into these qualities at scale; a Text subfamily reduces contrast and condenses slightly for sustained reading. Six weights with matching italics cover Extended Latin and Cyrillic.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type describe Oceanic as taking its inspiration from the upright contrast of 18th and 19th-century fat faces, with unconventional details – letterforms that echo prehistoric oceanic creatures – alongside capitals designed to command attention with a sense of slight discomfort. The Display family plays up those qualities; the Text family pulls back the contrast and condenses for smaller sizes and continuous reading.

name: Oceanic Gothic
classification_notes: Early grotesque in the late 19th to early 20th century tradition. Designed as a sans-serif companion to the Oceanic serif family, carrying over distinctive letter details from Oceanic Display into a grotesque structure. Display-forward in its heavier weights but workable in text settings across the range. Variable font available.
summary: A well-crafted early grotesque from Paris-based Interval Type, designed as the sans-serif companion to the Oceanic serif family with six weights, matching italics and variable font support across extended Latin and Cyrillic.
description: Oceanic Gothic arrived in 2024 as the sans-serif arm of Ilya Naumoff's Oceanic collection, inheriting the distinctive letter details of Oceanic Display within a grotesque framework rooted in late 19th and early 20th century sans design. Twelve styles from Light to Poster, plus a variable font, give it genuine range for editorial and branding work. Extended Cyrillic support and its coordination with the Oceanic serif families make it a practical choice for multilingual typographic systems.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type describes Oceanic Gothic as a sans-serif counterpart to the Oceanic and Oceanic Text serif families, conceived to echo the distinctive letter forms of Oceanic Display and produce a unified typographic personality across the collection. Drawing from the first grotesques of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, it balances display confidence with legibility at text sizes.

name: Oceanic Grotesk
classification_notes: Neutral modernist grotesk in the mid-20th century European tradition. Designed explicitly as a metrically matched companion to the Oceanic serif family, sharing identical vertical metrics with Oceanic Text. Prioritises neutrality and simplicity over personality. Alternate characters for a, K and R offer modest variation. Distributed as static fonts and a variable font.
summary: A clean, neutral neo-grotesque built primarily as the sans-serif half of Interval Type's Oceanic system, sharing vertical metrics with its serif counterparts across six weights and full italic coverage.
description: Oceanic Grotesk takes its cues from mid-20th century European modernism, sitting closer to Swiss neutrality than to expressive display work. Its most practical asset is metric compatibility with Oceanic and Oceanic Text, meaning serif and sans can swap without reflow. Six weights plus italics, Condensed and Compact subfamilies sold separately, and an included variable font round out a well-organised system with Extended Latin and Cyrillic coverage across 41 languages.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type is a Paris-based foundry focusing on Latin and Cyrillic typefaces. Oceanic Grotesk was created as a sans-serif companion to the Oceanic serif families, establishing a cohesive personality without replicating individual letterforms. The design draws from the modernist typographic tradition of the mid-20th century, with neutrality and simplicity as its stated core values. Desktop, web, app and trial licences are available with tiered pricing.

name: Oceanic Grotesk Compact
classification_notes: Compact-width grotesque within the Oceanic Collection, drawing on mid-20th-century modernist type values. Sits between the standard Oceanic Grotesk and the narrower Oceanic Grotesk Condensed in terms of horizontal compression. Shares identical vertical metrics with Oceanic Text, enabling consistent mixed serif/sans setting without metric adjustments.
summary: A compact-width grotesque from Ilya Naumoff's Oceanic Collection, built on mid-century modernist principles and calibrated to share vertical metrics with the accompanying Oceanic Text serif.
description: Oceanic Grotesk Compact is the narrow cut in Interval Type's Oceanic family, sitting between the standard-width Oceanic Grotesk and the more compressed Condensed. It applies the same modernist neutrality as its sibling but in a tighter frame suited to space-constrained layouts. Six weights from Light to Poster, matching italics, extended Latin and Cyrillic coverage and a variable font format give it genuine range across both text and display use.
foundry_blurb: Oceanic Grotesk Compact is a space-saving sans companion to the Oceanic serif family, sharing identical vertical metrics with Oceanic Text for consistent mixed use in body copy and titles. It covers extended Latin and Cyrillic across six weights with matching italics, and is also available as a variable font. The Compact width sits between standard Oceanic Grotesk and the narrower Condensed, giving designers a graduated set of options within the same system.

name: Oceanic Grotesk Condensed
classification_notes: Neutral, upright condensed grotesque drawing on mid-20th century modernist principles. Designed as a companion to the Oceanic serif superfamily, sharing identical vertical metrics with Oceanic Text. Variable font available alongside static instances.
summary: A condensed neutral grotesque from Paris-based Interval Type, designed as a companion to the Oceanic serif family with matching vertical metrics across six weights and a variable font.
description: Oceanic Grotesk Condensed takes its cues from mid-century modernist type: neutral, upright and space-efficient. Six weights from Light to Poster, each with a matching italic, give it range across body text and display work. Shared vertical metrics with Oceanic Text make it a natural fit within the wider Oceanic collection, and variable font support adds deployment flexibility.
foundry_blurb: Conceived as a sans companion to the Oceanic and Oceanic Text serif families, Oceanic Grotesk Condensed draws on the neutrality and simplicity of mid-20th century modernist typography. Six weights with matching italics span Light to Poster, supported by a variable font, with Extended Latin and Cyrillic script coverage. It shares identical vertical metrics with Oceanic Text, making it straightforward to mix serif and sans in the same layout.

name: Oceanic Text
classification_notes: High-contrast serif in the fat face tradition, referencing Bodoni, Canon and Scotch Roman. The Text subfamily reduces contrast and applies a slight condensation relative to the Display variant, making the design viable at reading sizes while retaining distinctively biomorphic letterforms – particularly the lowercase c and e. Supports extended Latin and Cyrillic.
summary: A text-optimised high-contrast serif with roots in 19th-century fat faces, disciplined for continuous reading without losing its distinctive biomorphic character.
description: Oceanic Text is Interval Type's text-weight companion to their expressive display serif, drawing on the upright contrast of fat faces in the tradition of Bodoni and Scotch Roman. The text subfamily reduces contrast and applies a slight condensation, making it genuinely usable at reading sizes while retaining the quirky letterforms – most notably the lowercase c and e, which echo prehistoric sea creatures. Extended Latin and Cyrillic support make it well-suited to multilingual editorial work.
foundry_blurb: Oceanic draws on the upright contrast of 18th and 19th-century fat faces like Bodoni, Canon and Scotch Roman, with unconventional details that reference prehistoric oceanic forms. The Text family reduces contrast and applies a slight condensation to create a quieter, more readable version of the display personality – one that integrates into both classic and contemporary editorial contexts.

name: Oceanic Text Mono
classification_notes: Monospaced serif drawing from 18th and 19th-century fat-face traditions – Bodoni, Canon and Scotch Romans. Contrast is reduced and proportions are slightly condensed versus the display cut to suit continuous reading and code. Letterforms carry deliberate strangeness: c and e evoke prehistoric oceanic creatures; R and K are intentionally dissonant with the rest of the alphabet. Fixed-width structure throughout. Part of the broader Oceanic family alongside Display and Text cuts.
summary: A monospaced serif rooted in fat-face tradition, with letterforms strange enough to stop the eye yet disciplined enough to hold up in code and technical documents.
description: Oceanic Text Mono is the fixed-width member of the Oceanic family, adapting the display variant's eccentric details for coding, tabular data and continuous text. Contrast is dialled down and proportions sit slightly narrower than the display cut, pulling the idiosyncrasy into a readable range across four weights. The lowercase c and e recall prehistoric sea creatures, R and K sit in deliberate tension with the rest of the alphabet, and it still functions.
foundry_blurb: Oceanic Text Mono preserves the idiosyncratic details of the broader Oceanic family within a fixed-width structure built for coding, tabular data and technical documents. It draws from the upright contrast of 18th and 19th-century fat faces – Bodoni, Canon, Scotch Romans – and incorporates unconventional forms: a c and e that recall prehistoric oceanic creatures, and capitals R and K designed to sit in slight discomfort with their surroundings.

name: Riegla
classification_notes: Non-neutral grotesk rooted in early 19th-century pre-rationalisation sans-serif tradition, citing Figgins Sans, Breite Grotesk and contemporaneous Gothics as references. Emphasises contrast and distinctiveness rather than the neutrality of mid-century grotesks. Designed as a companion to the fusion serif Riegraf, the two sharing structural commonalities for system use.
summary: A historically grounded non-neutral grotesk drawing on pre-rationalisation 19th-century sans-serif types, with three stylistic alternate sets and a companion serif for system use.
description: Riegla takes its references from early sans types including Figgins Sans and Breite Grotesk, favouring contrast and character over mid-century neutrality. Ten weights with italics give solid range across text and display settings, while Jazz and Classic alternate sets let the typeface shift register without switching family. It was released alongside the companion fusion serif Riegraf, the two sharing enough structural DNA to pair naturally across a page.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type describe Riegla as a multifunctional non-neutral grotesk drawing on early 19th-century sans-serif designs including Figgins Sans, Breite Grotesk and various Gothics of that era, with emphasis on the contrast and distinctiveness of the pre-rationalisation period. It was conceived as a companion to Riegraf, a fusion serif, with both released under the shared typefriends.com microsite.

name: Riegraf
classification_notes: High-contrast serif with simple square slab serifs. Deliberately shifts to low contrast in numerals and currency symbols, which read closer to a grotesk than a conventional serif. Self-described as a "geometric fusion serif". Designed as a typographic companion to Riegla, Interval Type's geometric grotesk.
summary: A geometric fusion serif that pairs high-contrast square slab letterforms with deliberately low-contrast numerals, designed as a companion to the grotesk Riegla.
description: Riegraf carries square slab serifs and high contrast in its letters, then pulls back to low contrast in numerals and currency symbols – a deliberate shift that grounds the typeface somewhere between classical serif tradition and geometric sans sensibility. Ten styles with matching italics run from Light to Black, with Latin Extended and Cyrillic coverage. It works well as a system with Riegla, Interval Type's companion grotesk, the two families sharing enough formal DNA to hold a page together.
foundry_blurb: Riegraf grew from the idea of designing a serif that feels like a geometric grotesk. The square slab serifs and high-contrast letterforms bring the elegance of the serif tradition, while low-contrast numerals and currencies recall the sans-serif world. Together with Riegla, the two families share enough commonalities to create typographic pairings that truly stand out.

name: Rooftop
classification_notes: American grotesque revival filtered through humanist proportions, with distinctively squarish ovals and sturdy stroke construction drawing on Lining Gothic and Gothic No. 2 as historical references. Six widths, three-axis variable font, and a Mono subfamily make it an unusually complete system for the genre.
summary: A squarish humanist grotesque rooted in early American Gothic tradition, built out across six widths with eight weights, italics, a Mono companion and a three-axis variable font.
description: Rooftop takes the sturdy construction of Lining Gothic and related early 20th-century American grotesques as its starting point, pairing that geometry with humanist proportions and distinctively squared ovals. The family is unusually complete: six widths from Ultra Condensed to Extended, eight weights per width each with matching italics, a dedicated Mono subfamily, and a three-axis variable font spanning weight, slant and width in a single file. Extended Latin and Cyrillic are supported throughout.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type describes Rooftop as drawing from American grotesques of the early 20th century with a humanist approach to construction, landing on what they call a contemporary tech-startup vibe. Slightly squarish curves and sturdy letterforms give the face a sense of technological sophistication aimed at modern brands and digital products.

name: Rooftop Mono
classification_notes: Monospaced typeface rooted in early 20th-century American grotesque tradition – specifically Lining Gothic (Barnhart Bros. & Spindler) and Gothic No. 2 (Palmer & Ray). Applies humanist grotesque construction to a fixed-pitch context, with slightly squarish curves and squared ovals that read as technical without being mechanical. Certain letterforms (f, t, r, g, y) take a deliberately structural, near-brutal approach. Part of the wider Rooftop collection by Paris-based Interval Type, but the mono stands alone as a 3-weight companion aimed at code and UI use.
summary: A monospaced grotesque grounded in early American gothic type traditions, with squarish curves and a deliberate structural character suited to code and technical interfaces.
description: Rooftop Mono draws from early 20th-century American grotesques – Lining Gothic from Barnhart Bros. & Spindler and Gothic No. 2 from Palmer & Ray – producing a fixed-pitch typeface with a squarish, technical edge. Certain letterforms (f, t, r, g, y) take a direct, constructivist approach that gives the font an assertive presence in code editors and UI contexts. Three weights cover most functional needs, with Cyrillic support alongside extended Latin across 32 languages.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type presents Rooftop Mono as a humanist grotesque brought into a contemporary tech setting: slightly squarish curves, squared ovals, and a structural treatment of key letterforms that sits somewhere between heritage American gothic and the visual language of modern software.

name: Stravinsky
classification_notes: Grafts Didot-style high vertical contrast and squarish counters onto a Grotesque sans-serif skeleton. The result is a hybrid display face with no serifs in the conventional sense but strong optical tension drawn from the Didone tradition. Stylistic alternates can introduce Didot serif elements, shifting it further along the spectrum toward a high-contrast serif display at the designer's discretion.
summary: A six-weight display sans from Paris-based Interval Type that applies Didot's extreme vertical contrast and squarish counters to a grotesque skeleton, with optional Didot serif alternates and full Cyrillic support.
description: Stravinsky sits in the contested territory between Didone and Grotesque, taking the high-contrast stress and tightly-set counters of 18th-century Didot and pressing them into a sans-serif structure. Designed by Ilya Naumoff at Interval Type in Paris, it spans six weights from Extralight to Extrabold and supports both extended Latin and Cyrillic. Stylistic alternates let designers toggle Didot serifs on or off, giving the face a second life as something closer to a classical high-contrast display serif.
foundry_blurb: Interval Type describes Stravinsky as a display face that fuses 18th-century Didot vertical contrast and squarish counters with the contemporary sans-serif Grotesk form. They characterise it as slightly chaotic and experimental but governed by a hidden order – a typeface suited to highlighting, teasing and saying things upfront, one that can read as traditional or daringly fresh depending on how it is paired.
